mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 1 Series 118d engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series 118d engine replacement typically costs £1,250-£2,800 for a reconditioned or rebuilt unit supply-only, depending on the engine code. With supply and fit, expect £2,300-£3,800 depending on the specialist and location.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 118d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common warning signs of N47 timing chain failure in a BMW 1 Series 118d include a rattling noise from the engine on cold start, rough idling, poor engine performance, and in later stages, the engine management light illuminating.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 1 Series 118d?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 2007-2015 BMW 1 Series 118d is typically valued at £2,700-£5,200. If your 118d is worth under £4,000, a full rebuilt engine may not be economically viable - consider a used engine or scrap the car. If your car is worth £5,500+ (low mileage, M Sport spec, good condition), a reconditioned engine with warranty is a sound investment.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 1 Series 118d engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series 118d engine replacement typically takes 2-3 days for a specialist to complete, including removal of the old unit and fitting the replacement. Timing chain replacement alone (without full engine removal) can be completed in 1-2 days.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 118d and 120d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the BMW 118d and 120d use the same 2.0-litre diesel engine family but with different power outputs. The 118d produces 122-150 hp depending on generation, while the 120d produces more power (up to 190 hp in later models).

mainEntity.name: Does a BMW 1 Series 118d rebuilt engine come with a warranty?

This covers the engine against manufacturing defects and component failure, giving you peace of mind when investing in a replacement M47, N47 or B47 unit.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 1 Series 118d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 118d has been the core diesel model across three generations of the 1 Series in the UK. Launched with the first-generation E87 in 2004, it has evolved through the N47 and B47 engine families - always using a 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbo diesel that offers the perfect balance of performance and economy. The 118d badge represents the diesel sweet spot in the 1 Series range, delivering strong torque and excellent fuel efficiency without the running costs of the more powerful 120d.

milestones.description: M47N2, 2.0L turbo diesel, 122 hp, launched with the E87 five-door and E81 three-door 1 Series
N47D20A / N47D20B, 2.0L turbo diesel, 143 hp, introduced with the E87/E81 LCI update
N47D20C / N47D20D, 2.0L turbo diesel, 143 hp, carried over into the second-generation F20/F21 1 Series
B47D20A, 2.0L turbo diesel (Euro 6), 150 hp, introduced as part of the F20/F21 LCI update
F40 generation launches with B47C20A, 2.0L turbo diesel, 150 hp, continuing the 118d badge
Current F70 generation continues with updated B-series diesel engines

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 1 Series 118d is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

items.title: 2.0L Turbo Diesel (2004-2007)
items.commonFailure: The M47 is generally more reliable than its successor, but high-mileage examples can suffer from turbocharger wear and injector issues. Regular oil changes are critical - the timing chain is at the front of the engine and more accessible than on the N47.

items.title: 2.0L Turbo Diesel (2007-2011)
items.commonFailure: The N47 engine family is notoriously prone to timing chain tensioner and guide failure. The original tensioner was too short, allowing the chain to become slack and rub against the guides. The timing chain is positioned at the rear of the engine, away from regular service reach, making inspection and replacement more labour-intensive. Typical failure mileage: 60,000-100,000 miles.

items.commonFailure: Same timing chain tensioner and guide issues as earlier N47 variants. The rear-mounted chain design remains a significant weakness. commonProblems.h2: BMW 1 Series 118d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 1 Series 118d has been powered by four different diesel engines across its production life. Early cars (2004-2007) use the M47N2 - a generally reliable unit with fewer major failure points. The N47D20 engines (2007-2015) are infamous for timing chain failure - a well-documented weakness that has affected countless BMW diesel owners. Later B47-powered cars (2015-present) are more reliable, with the timing chain moved to the front of the engine, but they have their own issues including oil leaks and EGR problems. Replacement demand for the BMW 118d is driven primarily by N47 timing chain failure. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner & Guide Failure - Why the BMW 1 Series 118d N47 Engine Fails Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The timing chain system on the N47 engine is positioned at the rear, away from regular service reach. The original tensioner was too short, allowing the chain to become slack and rub against the guides. When the timing chain does snap, it causes catastrophic engine failure - the pistons lose timing and hit the valves, bending them and damaging the rocker arms.

repairOptions.longevity: Best if caught early - rattle present but engine still running

This places the 118d in the "repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit" bracket for lower-value examples. If your 118d is worth under £4,000 and the engine has suffered catastrophic timing chain failure, evaluate scrap value first - replacement cost may approach or exceed the car's market value. For well-maintained, higher-spec examples (M Sport, low mileage, later generation) worth £5,500+, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine with warranty is a viable investment.

An £800-£1,300 specialist timing chain replacement is far cheaper than a full engine rebuild. If the chain has already snapped, the repair bill often exceeds the car's value - in that scenario, compare rebuilt engine prices through EnginesMarket against the cost of replacing the car. For owners planning to keep their 118d for 2+ years, a reconditioned N47 with upgraded timing components and warranty offers genuine peace of mind.

problems.h4: Oil Leaks & Injector Problems - B47 Engine
problems.rootCause: The B47 engine has been reported to suffer from oil leaks, particularly around the oil filter housing and the turbocharger. Fuel injector problems can also occur, leading to rough idling and decreased performance.

Address oil leaks promptly to prevent more serious damage. For injector issues, replace faulty components individually - this is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement.

problems.h4: EGR Cooler & DPF Issues - N47 and B47 Engines
problems.rootCause: The EGR system on BMW diesel engines can suffer from cooler failure and carbon buildup. Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) problems can arise, especially if the vehicle is primarily used for short trips where the DPF cannot complete its regeneration cycle.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace EGR cooler and related components
repairOptions.longevity: Check if your vehicle is covered by the BMW recall first
If DPF warning light is on and forced regeneration fails

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new components
repairOptions.longevity: If EGR or DPF failure has caused secondary damage

problems.recommendation: Before paying for any EGR-related repair on your BMW 1 Series 118d, check whether your vehicle is affected by the BMW diesel recall. BMW recalled 1.6 million diesel vehicles globally over concerns about faulty EGR coolers posing a potential fire risk. If your car is affected, the repair may be free of charge at a main dealer. For DPF issues, ensure you're giving your diesel 118d regular motorway runs to allow the DPF to regenerate. If the DPF warning light persists, professional cleaning is significantly cheaper than replacement.

finalCta.h4: Don't Let Engine Failure Write Off Your BMW 1 Series 118d
finalCta.paragraph: The N47 engine in your BMW 118d has a well-known timing chain weakness - but with the right specialist, this can be addressed before catastrophic failure occurs. Later B47-powered cars are more reliable but still benefit from regular maintenance and vigilance for oil leaks and EGR issues.
